       Re:     Notice of Non-Material Change in Status and Request for

               Gavin Power, LLC, Docket No. ER17-242-__

Dear Secretary Reese:

         Pursuant to Section 35.42 of the rules and regulations of the Federal Energy
Regulatory Commission (“Commission”), 1 Gavin Power, LLC (“Gavin”) hereby submits
for filing this notice of change in status (“Notice”). This Notice informs the Commission
that through its upstream owner, ECP ControlCo, LLC (“ECP”), Gavin has become
affiliated with Iron Senergy, LLC (“Iron Senergy”), which owns the Cumberland Mine, a
coal mine located in Greene County, Pennsylvania (the “Cumberland Mine”). 2 As
discussed below and in the affidavit of Ms. Solomon and Dr. Opgrand, 3 the changes
reported herein do not materially alter the facts upon which the Commission relied in
granting market-based rate authority to Gavin. Accordingly, Gavin respectfully requests
that the Commission accept this Notice without further inquiry.

II.       DESCRIPTION OF GAVIN

Commission’s regulations, 6 an asset appendix has been generated in the relational
database for Gavin (the “Gavin Asset Appendix”), which is incorporated herein by
reference. 7 A description of Gavin and its upstream ownership is set forth below.

          A.       Gavin

        Gavin owns a two-unit, coal-fired generating station located in Cheshire, Ohio,
with a summer net capacity rating of 2,709 MW. Gavin is an exempt wholesale generator
(“EWG”) 8 within the PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) balancing authority area

III.      NOTICE OF CHANGE IN STATUS

          A.       Additional Affiliation

        On September 2, 2026, an affiliate of ECP completed a transaction to acquire Iron
Senergy, which owns the Cumberland Mine. As a result, Gavin is now affiliated with a
new input to power production as defined in Section 35.36(a)(4) of the Commission’s
regulations. 16

          B.       Gavin Continues to Satisfy the Criteria for Market-Based Rate
                   Authority

        The Commission authorizes a seller to make wholesale sales of electric energy,
capacity, and ancillary services at market-based rates if the seller can demonstrate that it
and its affiliates: (i) do not possess, or have adequately mitigated, generation market
power in the relevant markets; (ii) do not possess, or have adequately mitigated, market
power in transmission; and (iii) do not control any other barriers to entry in the relevant



15

          purpose entity formed solely for the purpose of developing, financing, constructing,
          owning, and operating the Ten West Link transmission project, a 500 kV transmission
          line connecting substations in Tonopah, Arizona, and Riverside, California. The
          California Independent System Operator (“CAISO”) awarded DCRT the concession to
          build, finance, operate, and maintain the project in December 2015. DCRT is a joint
          venture between the Lotus Infrastructure Group and Atlantica DCR LLC. DCRT
          currently has a transmission owner tariff on file with the Commission. See DCR
          Transmission, L.L.C., 187 FERC ¶ 61,057 (2024). The Ten West Link project’s operation

          Energy Inc. (“Pivot”) and Convergent Energy and Power, Inc. (“Convergent”), each of

          the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 and the Commission’s implementing
          regulations thereunder, which are exempt from Section 205 of the Federal Power Act

markets. 17 As shown below, Gavin continues to satisfy each of the Commission’s criteria
for market-based rate authorization.

                   1.      Gavin Continues to Lack Horizontal Market Power

         Gavin continues to lack horizontal market power in the PJM market, which is the
market in which it is located. In Order No. 861, the Commission modified its regulations
to relieve certain sellers in Regional Transmission Organization (“RTO”) or Independent
System Operator (“ISO”) markets of the obligation to submit indicative screens to the
Commission in order to retain authority to sell electric energy, capacity, and specified
ancillary services at market-based rates. Specifically, the Commission removed the
obligation to submit indicative market power screens demonstrating a market-based rate
seller lacks horizontal market power in RTO/ISO-administered electric energy, ancillary
services, and capacity markets that are subject to Commission-approved RTO/ISO
monitoring and mitigation, including the PJM market. 18 Therefore, pursuant to
Section 35.37(c)(4) of the Commission’s regulations, 19 Gavin states that although it does
not have any horizontal market power in the relevant market, it is relying on
Commission-approved market monitoring and mitigation to address any potential
horizontal market power Gavin may have in the PJM market.

         As demonstrated herein, the new affiliation through ECP does not raise any
concern with respect to horizontal market power. Moreover, Gavin affirms that it has not
erected and will not erect barriers to entry into any geographic market. In light of the
facts and representations set forth in this Notice, the changes reported herein do not give
rise to any horizontal market power concerns.

                   2.      Gavin Continues to Lack Vertical Market Power

        To determine if a market-based rate seller has vertical market power, the
Commission will consider whether the seller and its affiliates have transmission market
power and whether they can erect other barriers to entry. 20 As explained herein, and as
further supported in the Secretariat Affidavit, 21 Gavin lacks vertical market power and
cannot, and will not, erect any barriers to entry.

                          a.         Transmission

         As noted above, Gavin is affiliated with DCRT. However, such affiliation does
not raise any vertical market power concerns because service on the transmission
facilities owned by DCRT is provided pursuant to CAISO’s Commission-approved Open
Access Transmission Tariff. Further, Gavin owns and operates a generation facility
located in the PJM BAA across the country from the CAISO BAA. Except for DCRT,
neither Gavin nor its affiliates, including Iron Senergy, owns or controls any electric
transmission facilities in the United States or outside the United States that can be used to
reach markets in the United States, except for the limited and discrete equipment
necessary to interconnect individual generation facilities to the transmission grid. Gavin
affirms that it and its affiliates (other than DCRT) that own or control limited and discrete
interconnection facilities qualify for the blanket open access transmission tariff waiver
pursuant to Section 35.28(d)(2) of the Commission’s regulations. 22 Gavin (and its
affiliates) lack market power with respect to transmission and, accordingly, the
Commission should find that Gavin continues to satisfy the Commission’s requirements
regarding transmission market power concerns.

                          b.         Inputs to Electric Power Production

        To demonstrate a lack of vertical market power through the ownership or control
of inputs to electric power production, a seller must provide a description of: (a) its
ownership or control of, or affiliation with an entity that owns or controls, intrastate
natural gas transportation, intrastate natural gas storage, or distribution facilities; and (b)
physical coal supply sources and ownership of or control over entities who may access
transportation of coal supplies. 23 A seller must also make an affirmative statement that it
and its affiliates have not erected, and will not erect, barriers to entry into the relevant
market. 24

       The only affiliation that Gavin has to entities that control inputs to electric power
production is through ECP’s interest in Iron Senergy, which owns the Cumberland Mine
and supplies coal to generating facilities, including in the PJM market. 25

        In Order No. 697, the Commission adopted a rebuttable presumption that
ownership or control of, or affiliation with an entity that owns or controls, intrastate
natural gas transportation, intrastate natural gas storage or distribution facilities, sites for
generation capacity development, and sources of coal supplies and the transportation of

The Commission has not found such ownership, control, or affiliation to be a potential
barrier to entry warranting further analysis in market-based rate proceedings.

       Accordingly, the Commission presumes that Gavin’s affiliation with Iron
Senergy, which owns sources of coal supplies, does not, in the absence of evidence to the
contrary, allow Gavin or its affiliates to raise entry barriers or otherwise raise vertical
market power concerns that would impact Gavin’s continued authority to make sales at
market-based rates.

        Notwithstanding the foregoing presumption, to provide the Commission with a
complete record and to affirmatively demonstrate that no competitive concerns arise from
this new affiliation, this Notice and the Secretariat Affidavit also demonstrate that
Gavin’s new affiliation with the Cumberland Mine does not allow Gavin or its affiliates
to raise barriers to entry. The Commission has found that even when an upstream supplier
provides more than a de minimis share of fuel inputs to power generation and an affiliated
company owns or controls more than a de minimis share of downstream generation
capacity, it is necessary for both the upstream (fuel supply) and downstream (electric
energy) markets to be highly concentrated before anticompetitive effects are likely. 27 As
the Secretariat Affidavit demonstrates, the upstream coal supply market is not highly
concentrated in PJM or PJM West, and neither PJM nor PJM West is a highly
concentrated generation market. 28

         Further, even if such markets were concentrated (which they are not), the
Secretariat Affidavit demonstrates that the Cumberland Mine coal supplies represent a de
minimis share of net generation in each of the PJM market and PJM West submarket
where ECP is affiliated with generation. 29 Gavin and its affiliates represent a small
generation market share (no greater than two percent) in each of the PJM market and
PJM West submarket, which further confirms that Gavin and its affiliates would not have
the incentive, or ability, to raise downstream rivals’ input costs. 30 Accordingly, Gavin’s
affiliation with the Cumberland Mine does not raise any vertical market power
concerns. 31

              AFFIDAVIT OF JULIE R. SOLOMON AND JEFFREY J. OPGRAND

INTRODUCTION

          My name is Julie R. Solomon. I am a Managing Director at Secretariat Advisors LLC
(“Secretariat”), an economic consulting firm located at 2121 K Street, NW, Washington, DC. A
large portion of my consulting activities involves electric utility industry restructuring and the
transition from regulation to competition. I have been involved extensively in consulting on market
power issues concerning mergers, other asset transactions, and market rate applications. I often file
affidavits before the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”) in connection with
electric utility mergers, the purchase and sale of jurisdictional assets, applications for market-based
rates, and triennial updates. My resume is included as Exhibit SEC-1.

          My name is Jeffrey J. Opgrand, PhD. I am a Director at Secretariat specializing in issues
pertaining to the energy industry. I have filed affidavits before the Commission in connection with
electric utility mergers, the purchase and sale of jurisdictional assets, and applications for market-
based rates. I was formerly an economist in the Office of Energy Policy and Innovation at the
Commission, where I worked on issues affecting wholesale electric markets, including financial
transmission rights and capacity markets. My resume is included as Exhibit SEC-2.

          We have been asked to provide an analysis in connection with a change in status (“CIS”)
arising from Gavin Power, LLC’s (“Gavin”) affiliation with Iron Senergy, LLC (“Iron Senergy”).
An affiliate of Gavin through ECP ControlCo, LLC (“ECP”) acquired Iron Senergy in September
2026. Iron Senergy owns the Cumberland coal mine located in Greene County, Pennsylvania (the
“Cumberland Mine”). 1


1
      The Cumberland Mine also includes a 17-mile short-line railway that transports clean coal from Iron Senergy’s
      preparation plant in Kirby, PA to Alicia Harbor, located in Alicia, PA.


                                                         1
           We note at the outset that in Order No. 697, the Commission adopted a rebuttable
presumption that ownership or control of, or affiliation with an entity that owns or controls,
intrastate natural gas transportation, intrastate natural gas storage or distribution facilities, sites for
generation capacity development, sources of coal supplies and the transportation of coal supplies
such as barges and rail cars, do not allow a seller to raise entry barriers. 2 Accordingly, the
Commission should presume that Gavin’s affiliation with Iron Senergy, which owns sources of
coal supplies and a short-line rail system to transport such supplied within Pennsylvania, does not,
in the absence of evidence to the contrary, allow Gavin or its affiliates to raise entry barriers or
otherwise raise vertical market power concerns that would impact their continued authority to
make sales at market-based rates. In other words, the new affiliation with Iron Senergy has no
effect on Gavin’s continued eligibility to make sales at market-based rates. Nevertheless, to
provide the Commission with a complete record and to affirmatively demonstrate that no
competitive concerns arise from this affiliation, our analysis shows that Gavin’s affiliation with
the Cumberland Mine does not create any adverse competitive effects in any relevant market.

        This CIS does not involve any horizontal combination of electric generating assets, and
Gavin continues to satisfy the Commission’s horizontal market power screens in each relevant
market. The only relevant analysis in evaluating this CIS is whether there are vertical market
power effects that may arise from combining the ownership and/or affiliation of inputs to electric
power production (i.e., coal supply) with the electric generating assets owned by Gavin and its
ECP affiliates. 3 As set forth herein, no such effects are present.

        Sellers with market rate authority are required to report a change (such as the acquisition
of transmission or generation over 100 megawatts or a new affiliation with an entity owning or
controlling such assets or the inputs to such assets) by filing a Notice of CIS consistent




2
    Market-Based Rates for Wholesale Sales of Elec. Energy, Capacity & Ancillary Servs. By Pub. Utils., Order No.
    697, 119 FERC ¶ 61,295 at P 22 (2007) (“Order No. 697”).
3
    The Commission, under 18 C.F.R. § 35.42, requires that “a Seller must timely report to the Commission any change
    in status that would reflect a departure from the characteristics the Commission relied upon in granting market-based
    rate authority.” Of relevance here is Gavin’s new affiliation with the Cumberland Mine, which constitutes an inputs
    to electric power production pursuant to Section 35.36(a)(4) of the Commission’s regulations.


                                                           2
 with Commission Order Nos. 652, 816, 697, 860, and 18 C.F.R. § 35.42. The change here arises
because ECP acquired control of inputs to generation in the form of coal supplies.

        A transaction that combines a downstream electric wholesale business (e.g., Gavin or other
ECP generation affiliates) with an entity that owns or controls upstream fuel supply (e.g., Iron
Senergy) could, in theory, potentially raise a competitive concern that control over upstream inputs
(e.g., coal) vital to the downstream market (e.g., generation) may provide the integrated company
the incentive and ability to raise input costs to rival electric power generators. Under some specific
fact situations—not present here—raising fuel costs of rival generation companies could result in
an increase in wholesale electric energy prices such that the acquiring company would receive
higher prices and profits from wholesale electric energy sales than it would earn otherwise. This
theory is often referred to as “vertical foreclosure” or “raising rivals’ costs,” and is one of the
primary competitive concerns addressed by the Commission in mergers or transactions of
companies owning electric generation with fuel supply companies. 4 However, our analysis
indicates that the factual circumstances here do not support any such concern.

        As we demonstrate below, there is no adverse effect on vertical competition in any relevant
wholesale electricity market as a result of the CIS. Indeed, the impact is de minimis in the relevant
markets. Gavin and its ECP affiliates therefore continue to satisfy the Commission’s requirements
for market-based rate authorization.

SUMMARY OF ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSIONS

        Coal from the Cumberland Mine is either delivered to geographic markets where ECP is
affiliated with a de minimis amount of generation; or the coal is delivered to industries other than
electric power generation for other uses.

        The relevant market for the Cumberland Mine’s coal supplies in the context of this CIS is
the PJM Interconnection L.L.C. (“PJM”) market and relevant submarkets, where ECP also owns

concentrated before anticompetitive effects are likely. 7                    We conduct an upstream market

concentrated (i.e., an HHI of 1,800 points or higher), which would lead the Commission to

is not highly concentrated in PJM or PJM West. Further, as we have previously demonstrated,
neither the PJM generation market, nor the PJM West generation submarket are highly
concentrated. 9

5.   All Privileged Material and/or CEII must be maintained in a secure place. Access
     to those materials must be limited to Reviewing Representatives specifically
     authorized pursuant to Paragraphs 7-9 of this Protective Agreement.

6.   Privileged Material and/or CEII must be handled by each Party and by each
     Reviewing Representative in accordance with the Non-Disclosure Certificate
     executed pursuant to Paragraph 9 of this Protective Agreement. Privileged
     Material and/or CEII shall not be used except as necessary for the conduct of this
     proceeding, nor shall they (or the substance of their contents) be disclosed in any
     manner to any person except a Reviewing Representative who is engaged in this
     proceeding and who needs to know the information in order to carry out that
     person’s responsibilities in this proceeding. Reviewing Representatives may
     make copies of Privileged Material and/or CEII, but such copies automatically
     become Privileged Material and/or CEII. Reviewing Representatives may make
     notes of Privileged Material, which shall be treated as Notes of Privileged
     Material if they reflect the contents of Privileged Material.

7.   If a Reviewing Representative’s scope of employment includes any of the
     activities listed under this Paragraph 7, such Reviewing Representative may not
     use information contained in any Privileged Material and/or CEII obtained in this
     proceeding for a commercial purpose (e.g., to give a Party or competitor of any
     Party a commercial advantage):

     A.     Energy marketing;
       B.     Direct supervision of any employee or employees whose duties include
             energy marketing; or

      C.     The provision of consulting services to any person whose duties include
             energy marketing.

8.    If a Party wishes to designate a person not described in Paragraph 3.E above as a
      Reviewing Representative, the Party must seek agreement from the Party
      providing the Privileged Material and/or CEII to treat such designee as a
      Reviewing Representative pursuant to Paragraph 3.E of this Protective Agreement
      with respect to those materials.

9.    A Reviewing Representative shall not be permitted to inspect, participate in
      discussions regarding, or otherwise be permitted access to Privileged Material
      and/or CEII pursuant to this Protective Agreement until three business days after
      that Reviewing Representative first has executed and served a Non-Disclosure
      Certificate. However, if an attorney qualified as a Reviewing Representative has
      executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate, any participating paralegal, secretarial and
      clerical personnel under the attorney’s instruction, supervision or control need not
      do so. Attorneys designated Reviewing Representatives are responsible for
      ensuring that persons under their supervision or control comply with this
      Protective Agreement, and must take all reasonable precautions to ensure that
      Privileged Material and/or CEII are not disclosed to unauthorized persons. All
      executed Non-Disclosure Certificates must be served on all Parties on the official
      service list maintained by the Secretary of the Commission for the proceeding.

10.   Any Reviewing Representative may disclose Privileged Material and/or CEII to
      any other Reviewing Representative as long as both Reviewing Representatives
      have executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate. In the event any Reviewing
      Representative to whom Privileged Material and/or CEII are disclosed ceases to
      participate in this proceeding, or becomes employed or retained for a position that
      renders him or her ineligible to be a Reviewing Representative under Paragraph
      3.E of this Protective Agreement, access to such materials by that person shall be
      terminated. Even if no longer engaged in this proceeding, every person who has
      executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate shall continue to be bound by the
      provisions of this Protective Agreement and the Non-Disclosure Certificate for as
      long as the Protective Agreement is in effect.

11.   All Privileged Material and/or CEII in this proceeding filed with the Commission,
      or submitted to any Commission personnel must comply with the Commission’s
      Notice of Document Labelling Guidance for Documents Submitted to or Filed
      with the Commission or Commission Staff. Consistent with those requirements:

      A.     Documents that contain Privileged Material must include a top center
             header on each page of the document with the following text: CUI//PRIV.
             Any corresponding electronic files must also include this text in the file
             name.
       B.     Documents that contain CEII must include a top center header on each
             page of the document with the following text: CUI//CEII. Any
             corresponding electronic files must also include this text in the file name.

      C.     Documents that contain both Privileged Material and CEII must include a
             top center header on each page of the document with the following text:
             CUI//CEII/PRIV. Any corresponding electronic files must also include
             this text in the file name.

      D.     The specific content on each page of the document that constitutes
             Privileged Material and/or CEII must also be clearly identified. For
             example, lines or individual words or numbers that include both Privileged
             Material and CEII shall be prefaced and end with “BEGIN
             CUI//CEII/PRIV” and “END CUI//CEII/PRIV”.

12.   Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall be construed as precluding any Party
      from objecting to the production or use of Privileged Material and/or CEII on any
      appropriate ground.

13.   Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall preclude any Party from requesting the
      Chief Judge, the Commission, or any other body having appropriate authority, to
      find this Protective Agreement should not apply to all or any materials previously
      designated Privileged Material pursuant to this Protective Agreement. The Chief
      Judge, the Commission, or any other body having appropriate authority may alter
      or amend this Protective Agreement as circumstances warrant at any time during
      the course of this proceeding.

14.   Each Party governed by this Protective Agreement has the right to seek changes
      in it as appropriate from the Chief Judge, the Commission, or any other body
      having appropriate authority.

15.   Subject to Paragraph 18, the Chief Judge or the Commission shall resolve any
      disputes arising under this Protective Agreement pertaining to Privileged Material
      according to the following procedures. Prior to presenting any such dispute to the
      Chief Judge or the Commission, the Parties to the dispute shall employ good faith
      best efforts to resolve it.

      A.     Any Party that contests the designation of material as Privileged Material
             shall notify the Party that provided the Privileged Material by specifying
             in writing the material for which the designation is contested.

      B.     In any challenge to the designation of material as Privileged Material, the
             burden of proof shall be on the Party seeking protection. If the Chief
             Judge, or the Commission finds that the material at issue is not entitled to
             the designation, the procedures of Paragraph 18 shall apply.

      C.     The procedures described above shall not apply to material designated by
             a Party as CEII. Material so designated shall remain subject to the
              provisions of this Protective Agreement unless a Party requests and
             obtains a determination from the Commission’s CEII Coordinator that
             such material need not retain that designation.

16.   The designator will have five (5) days in which to respond to any pleading
      requesting disclosure of Privileged Material. Should the Chief Judge, or the
      Commission, as appropriate, determine that the information should be made
      public, the Chief Judge, or the Commission will provide notice to the designator
      no less than five (5) days prior to the date on which the material will become
      public. This Protective Agreement shall automatically cease to apply to such
      material on the sixth (6th) calendar day after the notification is made unless the
      designator files a motion with the Chief Judge, or the Commission, as appropriate,
      with supporting affidavits, demonstrating why the material should continue to be
      privileged. Should such a motion be filed, the material will remain confidential
      until such time as the interlocutory appeal or certified question has been addressed
      by the Motions Commissioner or Commission, as provided in the Commission’s
      regulations, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.714, 385.715. No Party waives its rights to seek
      additional administrative or judicial remedies after a Chief Judge decision
      regarding Privileged Material or the Commission’s denial of any appeal thereof or
      determination in response to any certified question. The provisions of 18 C.F.R.
      §§ 388.112 and 388.113 shall apply to any requests under the Freedom of
      Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) for Privileged Material and/or CEII in the files
      of the Commission.

17.   Privileged Material and/or CEII shall remain available to Parties until the later of
      1) the date an order terminating this proceeding no longer is subject to judicial
      review, or 2) the date any other Commission proceeding relating to the Privileged
      Material and/or CEII is concluded and no longer subject to judicial review. After
      this time, the Party that produced the Privileged Material and/or CEII may request
      (in writing) that all other Parties return or destroy the Privileged Material and/or
      CEII. This request must be satisfied within fifteen (15) days of the date the
      request is made. However, copies of filings, official transcripts and exhibits in
      this proceeding containing Privileged Material, or Notes of Privileged Material,
      may be retained if they are maintained in accordance with Paragraph 5 of this
      Protective Agreement. If requested, each Party also must submit to the Party
      making the request an affidavit stating that to the best of its knowledge it has
      satisfied the request to return or destroy the Privileged Material and/or CEII. To
      the extent Privileged Material and/or CEII are not returned or destroyed, they
      shall remain subject to this Protective Agreement.

18.   Regardless of any order terminating this proceeding, this Protective Agreement
      shall remain in effect until specifically modified or terminated by the Parties. All
      CEII designations shall be subject to the “[d]uration of the CEII designation”
      provisions of 18 C.F.R. § 388.113(e).
